newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rights lawyers complain of harassment.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rights lawyers complain of harassment.

text.p: Indonesian human rights lawyers complained on Wednesday of continuing harassment by authorities in the wake of Jakarta's July riots, including attempts to make them provide information against their own clients.

Legal Aid Institute (LBH) chairman Bambang Widjojanto went to the attorney-general's office on Wednesday to protest against five summonses he had received to be a witness in the investigation of his own clients arrested after the riots.

"The various recent cases indeed show an increase in the level of surveillance and pressure to human rights lawyers, especially in the regions where human rights violations are high," Munir, head of the LBH's operations section, told Reuters.
He said LBH offices in Lampung in South Sumatra, Medan in North Sumatra and Surabaya in East Java had all recently been the subject of government intimidation.
On Tuesday, the office of leading human rights lawyer Johannes Princen was searched for four hours by nine officials from the attorney-general's office with a search warrant.
Princen told Reuters the government was trying to scare those lawyers, like himself, defending activists arrested after the riots.

Activists say the harassment of lawyers is part of a wider government pattern of pressure on critics and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) after the worst riots in the capital in more than 20 years saw at least five people die on July 27.

Earlier this month, more than 20 NGOs complained to the official National Commision on Human Rights about increasing harassment, raids and torture during interogation by security officials since the riots.

Police and the attorney-general's office have summoned a large number of critics and activists since July in a continuing investigation of members of the small left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD) which the government blames for the riots.
"This morning Bambang went to the attorney-general's office. He did not receive a summons," Munir said.
"He went there to explain a number of things including protest against the pattern of sumonses he had received as a witness and the treatment of the accused," Munir said.
Widjojanto has ignored five summonses to be questioned in the cases of independent labour leader Mucthar Pakpahan as well as PRD members Budiman Sudjatmiko and Petrus Haryanto.
All three men, who are being represented by a legal team which included Widjojanto, face subversion charges which carries a maximum penalty of death.
Widjonjanto, 1993 winner of the Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Award, told Reuters recently he would not answer the summonses as they were flawed and he could not testify against his clients.

The LBH has also complained to the national police chief about the questioning last week of its Ujung Pandang office head, Nasiruddin Pasigai, who was accused of trying to overthrow the government after he met last month with a U.S. academic.
Local reporters who met with Bill Liddle, professor of political science at the Ohio State University, were also questioned by police.
